name: Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen
overview: The state museum of North Rhine-Westphalia for art from the early twentieth century onward, in Düsseldorf, in two buildings: K20 at Grabbeplatz 5, by Dissing+Weitling, and K21 in the Ständehaus, the former state parliament building, converted by Kiessler Architekten (museum website; collection website).

Founded in 1961 as Stiftung Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen after the state bought 88 works by Paul Klee in 1960 from the collection of the American industrialist G. David Thompson; Werner Schmalenbach was founding director; K20 opened in 1986 and K21 in 2002 (collection website).

The collection: works by Beckmann, Braque, Ernst, Kirchner, Matisse, Mondrian, Picasso, Rauschenberg and Warhol, Jackson Pollock's Number 32 (1950, acquired 1964) and Joseph Beuys's Palazzo Regale (1985, acquired 1993); the Ackermans Collection of more than 150 works came in 2004 and the Fischer Collection of Minimal and Conceptual art between 2013 and 2015. The page gives no total and no purchase prices (collection website).
funding_verdict: Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen: mainly public, a state museum, plus corporate partners and foundations
wider_context: The collection website notes that Nazi authorities dismissed Paul Klee from the Düsseldorf Academy in 1933 and that his works were among those defamed as 'degenerate'; the state's 1960 purchase of 88 Klee works is the founding act of the collection (collection website).

name: BMW Museum
overview: The BMW Museum is the company museum of BMW in Munich, with houses on company history, design, technology and motorsport and an Art Car Gallery (BMW Welt page).
It opened on 18 May 1973, closed in 2004 for renovation and reopened in June 2008 (BMW newsroom).

What is there: 5,000 square metres of exhibition in seven themed houses with rotating special exhibitions; a temporary show, Belle Macchine, is listed until the end of 2026. The pages read gave no object or vehicle count (BMW newsroom, BMW Welt page).
funding_verdict: BMW Museum: paid by the company; no budget published on the pages read.

name: Residenztheater (Bayerisches Staatsschauspiel)
overview: The Bavarian State Theatre for spoken drama plays in three venues near the Munich Residenz: the Residenztheater on Max-Joseph-Platz with 881 seats, the Cuvilliéstheater with 437 seats and the Marstall with about 146 seats (theatre website).
It grew out of the princely court and national theatre of the 18th century; the royal court theatre became the Staatstheater after the revolution of 1918 (theatre website; German Wikipedia).
It is one of four Bavarian State Theatres in Munich, with the State Opera, the Theatre Academy August Everding at the Prinzregententheater and the Gärtnerplatztheater (theatre website).
funding_verdict: Residenztheater: public: the Free State of Bavaria, with a friends' association and foundations on single projects

name: Museum Abteiberg
overview: Municipal museum of contemporary art in the historic centre of Mönchengladbach, built into the face of a hillside next to the cathedral and a baroque abbey (hollein.com).
Called the Städtisches Museum Abteiberg. The city of Mönchengladbach was the client, planning ran 1972 to 1973 and the building was completed in 1982 (hollein.com).

Designed by the Austrian architect Hans Hollein. The building is a walk-on structure whose surface is open to the public and used for open-air sculpture, and the interior is a sequence of white spaces arranged as a three-dimensional matrix rather than a linear route (hollein.com).
funding_verdict: Museum Abteiberg: mainly public: the city of Mönchengladbach

name: Hong Kong Arts Festival
overview: The Hong Kong Arts Festival is a non-profit organisation launched in 1973 (festival website).
The pages read did not name a building or a founder.
What is there: the festival presents an annual programme; the 55th Festival and the 2027 No Limits programme fall in the 2026/27 budget (festival website).
funding_verdict: Hong Kong Arts Festival: mainly private: sponsorship and donations target about 44 percent, government baseline about 11 percent

name: Anu Museum of the Jewish People
aliases: Anu - Museum of the Jewish People
overview: The museum of the Jewish people, on Tel Aviv University's campus, formerly Beit Hatfutsot (AP via KOMO, 10 March 2021).
Reopened in March 2021 after more than a decade of renovation; exhibition space tripled to 72,000 square feet (AP via KOMO, 10 March 2021).

What is there: objects including a jawza instrument from the Al-Kuwaity brothers, a Ruth Bader Ginsburg collar, a pre-Inquisition Book of Esther scroll and a first-century carved stone from a Galilee synagogue (AP via KOMO, 10 March 2021). No total count was given.
funding_verdict: Anu Museum of the Jewish People: mixed, large private and US gifts plus an Israeli government share.

name: Museo Nazionale della Scienza e della Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci
aliases: Museo della Scienza e della Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci
Fondazione Museo nazionale della scienza e della tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci
overview: The Museo Nazionale della Scienza e della Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci is a museum in Milan, inaugurated on 15 February 1953 and run since 1 January 2000 as a private-law foundation (Corte dei conti report on 2024).

Its aim is the study and communication of the work of Leonardo da Vinci and of science and technology, through research, conservation and updating of its collections, archives and library (Corte dei conti report on 2024).

What is there: over 170 historic models, works of art, old volumes and installations about Leonardo, and a heritage of 15,000 technical-scientific and artistic objects, over 50,000 square metres, 15 exhibition sections and 13 interactive laboratories (Corte dei conti report on 2024).
funding_verdict: Museo Nazionale della Scienza e della Tecnologia: public money from three ministries and local bodies, plus a growing share from private fundraising.

name: Castello di Rivoli Museo d Arte Contemporanea
overview: Contemporary art museum in a former residence of the House of Savoy at Rivoli, near Turin. It opened as a museum in 1984 and is described by Wikipedia as the first contemporary art museum in Italy.

Castle history: first mentioned in 1159, used as barracks from 1863, heavily damaged in the Second World War and restored from 1979. Andrea Bruno was the architect of the first post-war renovation (Wikipedia). It is one of 14 Savoy residences on the UNESCO World Heritage list since 1997.

Directors: Rudi Fuchs and Johannes Gachnang (1984 to 1991), Ida Giannelli (1991 to 2008), Andrea Bellini and Beatrice Merz (2010 to 2014), Carolyn Christov-Bakargiev (2015 to 2024) and Francesco Manacorda from 2024 (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Castello di Rivoli: mainly public money plus two private foundations: Regione Piemonte, City of Turin, Town of Rivoli, Fondazione CRT and Compagnia di San Paolo

name: The Jordan Museum
overview: National museum of Jordan's archaeology and history in Amman's Ras Al Ain area, in a building of about 10,000 square metres (The Jordan Times, 12 February 2017; The National, 13 March 2014).

Director general Ihab Amarin said a Jordan Museum had been a national dream since the 1960s; its first phase, from the Palaeolithic to the end of the Classical period, opened in 2013 (The Jordan Times, 2017). The National reported a soft opening in January 2013, with Sharifa Nofa Bint Nasser as director.

A royal decree of 2002 established a national museum; Queen Rania, chair of the board of trustees, laid its cornerstone at Ras El Ein on 2 October 2005, after building work on the three-storey museum had begun that year (Jordan News, 13 April 2021; Office of Queen Rania, 3 October 2005). The chief architect was the late Jafar Tukan (Jordan News).
funding_verdict: The Jordan Museum: public: the Jordanian state, with a building paid for in part by a Japanese yen loan

name: Fondation H
overview: Contemporary art foundation in the centre of Antananarivo, at the foot of the Queen's Palace and the Prime Minister's palace (The Art Newspaper France, Anaël Pigeat, 23 June 2023).
Founded in 2017 by the entrepreneur and patron Hassanein Hiridjee, who is its president. Madagascar has recognised it as a public-utility foundation since 2018 (the foundation's website).
Hiridjee began the collection in 2010. Its about 200 works all belong to the foundation (The Art Newspaper France, 2023).
funding_verdict: Fondation H: private: founded and presided over by Axian chief executive Hassanein Hiridjee, with free entry

name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech
overview: Museum devoted to the work of fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent, on Rue Yves Saint Laurent near the Jardin Majorelle in Marrakech (Wikipedia; Fondation Jardin Majorelle press release, 15 November 2022).
Inaugurated in October 2017 and opened to the public on 19 October 2017 (Wikipedia).

Pierre Bergé said it was "natural to build a museum dedicated to the work of Yves Saint Laurent in Morocco" (Wikipedia). It shows the collection of the Pierre Bergé - Yves Saint Laurent Foundation. A second museum for the collection stands at the former fashion house headquarters in Paris (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech: privately funded: Pierre Bergé's sale of Moroccan art, run by the Fondation Jardin Majorelle

name: Fundación MAPFRE
overview: Exhibition halls at Paseo de Recoletos 23 in Madrid, of about 1,000 square metres, run by the culture area of Fundación MAPFRE, which also runs the KBr photography centre in Barcelona, opened in autumn 2020 (foundation website).

Fundación MAPFRE is a non-profit institution created by the insurer Mapfre, constituted on 5 November 1975 and classed as a private cultural foundation by the Ministry of Education and Science on 14 May 1976; its registered office is at Paseo de Recoletos 23 (annual accounts 2025).

What is there: three seasons a year of paired exhibitions of painting and photography, on international art from the mid 19th to the mid 20th century and on photographers of the 20th century and the present; the 2025 exhibitions in Madrid had 319,559 visitors (annual accounts 2025). The foundation's own collections hold more than 2,000 pieces, mainly drawings, prints and photographs, with photography added from 2007 (foundation website); the balance sheet carries them under 'Museos' at 20,360 thousand euros net, and 2025 purchases of 300 thousand euros went mainly on photographs by Eduardo Nave, María Linarejos, Jorge Yeregui, Paula Artés and Israel Ariño (annual accounts 2025).
funding_verdict: Fundación MAPFRE: private, paid from dividends of the insurer Mapfre S.A., which the foundation controls

name: CA2M Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo
aliases: centro de arte dos de mayo
CA2M (Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo)
overview: Contemporary art museum at Avenida de la Constitución 23 in central Móstoles, in the Comunidad de Madrid (Es Madrid).
Opened in May 2008 on the site of a traditional building called La Casona (Spanish Wikipedia).

Building of 5,886 square metres with exhibition rooms on three floors, a 100-seat auditorium, a library and a terrace. The basic architectural project is by Celia Vinuesa, executed by Pablo Pérez-Urruti, and since 2016 Andrés Jaque Studio, Office for Political Innovation, has carried out a series of "architectural acupuncture" interventions (Es Madrid).
funding_verdict: CA2M Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo: public: Comunidad de Madrid (regional government)

name: Usine Kugler (Fédération des Artistes de Kugler)
overview: Former tap factory in the Jonction area of Geneva, now artists' studios and exhibition and performance spaces. The Fonderie Kugler is at Avenue de la Jonction 19, 1205 Geneva (guide-contemporain.ch).

The Fédération des artistes de Kugler (FAK) is the federation of the artist associations based at the site: Kugler Est, Atelier Drozophile, Cheminée Nord, Espace Kugler, Kuglof, La Database59, L-Ouest, L-Sud and Verrière Sud (usinekugler.ch).

The Fonderie Kugler sits alongside about 220 active professional artists' studios, keeps its industrial architecture and has a 400 m2 modular space for artistic research and emerging arts. It is managed collectively through an office and run by the FAK (guide-contemporain.ch).
funding_verdict: Usine Kugler: self-managed artist federation; public bodies handle the site and list the Fonderie

name: Plateforme 10
overview: Plateforme 10 is an arts district beside Lausanne station that brings together, in the site's words, 3 canton-level museums and 2 foundations: the Musée cantonal des beaux-arts (MCBA), mudac and Photo Elysée (site).

The MCBA building was inaugurated in 2019; Photo Elysée and mudac moved in during 2022, and the site opened to the public on the weekend of 19 June 2022 with 30,000 visits across 25,000 square metres (site; Canton of Vaud press release).
What is there: the MCBA's permanent display includes some three hundred works from the eighteenth century to the present; the pages read gave no collection figures for mudac or Photo Elysée.
funding_verdict: Plateforme 10: public-private, the Canton of Vaud with private donors; operating funding not stated on the pages read

name: Montreux Jazz Festival
aliases: Claude Nobs Collection of the Montreux Jazz Festival
overview: The Montreux Jazz Festival has been held since 1967; its collection has brought together 5,000 concerts since then (EPFL).
Claude Nobs was its founder and director (EPFL).
What is there: the archive holds over 11,000 hours of video and 6,000 hours of audio, including multitrack, digitised and stored in three copies (EPFL).
funding_verdict: Montreux Jazz Festival: festival funding not stated on the pages read; archive paid for by named donors led by Audemars Piguet

name: Museum of Anatolian Civilizations
overview: Archaeology museum on the south side of Ankara Castle in the Atpazarı area of Ulus, Ankara (Wikipedia; Turkish Museums, Ministry of Culture and Tourism).
Began in 1921 when the culture director Mübarek Galip set up a museum in the Akkale bastion of the castle, at Atatürk's wish for a Hittite museum (Turkish Museums).

Housed in two Ottoman buildings, the Mahmut Paşa Bedesteni (covered bazaar) and the Kurşunlu Han, which the Culture and Tourism Minister dates to the reign of Mehmed II; the central hall opened to visitors in 1943, during the conversion (Turkish Museums; DHA, 21 July 2026).
funding_verdict: Museum of Anatolian Civilizations: state: Turkey's Ministry of Culture and Tourism
wider_context: A Court of Accounts (Sayıştay) audit found that the museum's asset codes for its objects did not match its inventory register, so a physical count could not easily locate an object, and that its storerooms lacked suitable size, temperature, light and humidity conditions (Sözcü, 2 October 2021).

name: Harry Ransom Center
overview: A humanities research library and museum at 300 West 21st Street on the UT Austin campus; the current building opened in 1972 and a $14.5 million renovation was completed in 2003 (HRC website).
Founded in 1957 by Harry Huntt Ransom, an English professor who later became chancellor of UT, as the Humanities Research Center (HRC website).

What is there: about 1 million books, more than 42 million manuscripts, 5 million photographs and 100,000 works of art. Named holdings include one of only 20 complete Gutenberg Bibles, Gabriel Garcia Marquez's manuscripts, correspondence and notebooks, digitized for viewing, and the Gernsheim Collection on the history of photography, acquired in 1963 (HRC website).
funding_verdict: Harry Ransom Center: mainly public, through the state university, plus endowment and private gifts
wider_context: In an opinion piece in the Austin American-Statesman on 10 March 2017, the Center's director, Stephen Enniss, wrote about the proposed elimination of the National Endowment for the Arts and the National Endowment for the Humanities, according to the Center's magazine (Ransom Center Magazine, 23 March 2017). The page read did not give the text of the argument.

name: Cincinnati Art Museum
overview: An art museum at 953 Eden Park Drive in Eden Park, Cincinnati, Ohio (museum website).
The Cincinnati Museum Association was incorporated on 15 February 1881 to build and run it, and it opened on 17 May 1886 (museum website).
The collection is more than 73,000 works covering 6,000 years, searchable online (museum website).
funding_verdict: Cincinnati Art Museum: private gifts and endowment return, with city, state and ArtsWave operating support

name: Frederik Meijer Gardens & Sculpture Park
overview: Frederik Meijer Gardens & Sculpture Park is in Grand Rapids, Michigan, on a 158-acre main campus with indoor galleries, gardens and a children's garden (The Art Newspaper, 6 October 2017; annual report 2025).
It opened in 1995 and by 2017 welcomed 750,000 visitors a year, nearly four times the number it was designed for (The Art Newspaper, 6 October 2017).

What is there: a sculpture collection with works by artists such as Georges Minne and Joel Shapiro, a Lena Meijer Tropical Conservatory and Japanese Garden, and an archive acquisition shown in an expanded indoor gallery (The Art Newspaper, 6 October 2017; annual report 2025).
funding_verdict: Frederik Meijer Gardens: earned income and contributions, with a $200 million endowment from the Meijer family circle

name: Hollywood Bowl
overview: The Hollywood Bowl is an outdoor concert venue in Los Angeles; Los Angeles County Parks and Recreation owns the venue and surrounding parkland and the LA Phil operates it (LA Phil presentation to the County, 1 October 2025).
The LA Phil's site lists the Hollywood Bowl and the Hollywood Bowl Orchestra among its venues (LA Phil website).

What is there: concerts across genres; over 1.3 million people attended in 2024 and the LA Phil plans pricing with 50 percent of 2026 tickets at $48 and under (LA Phil presentation to the County, 1 October 2025).
funding_verdict: Hollywood Bowl: county-owned land, run by the LA Phil; the Bowl's own revenue is not stated in the pages read

name: The New York Historical
overview: A history museum and research library at 170 Central Park West, Manhattan, in a building whose first portion was completed in 1908 and which was expanded on either side in 1938 (The Art Newspaper, 16 June 2026).
Founded in 1804 as the New-York Historical Society, it describes itself as New York City's first museum; it rebranded as the New York Historical in October 2024 (The Art Newspaper, 29 October 2024).

What is there: more than 14 million works of art, artifacts, documents and ephemera spanning four centuries of American history, with an American art collection, a folk art collection, sculptures by Elie Nadelman, fragments of the equestrian statue of George III toppled in 1776 and a broadside printing of the Declaration of Independence (New York State governor's release, June 2026; The Art Newspaper, 16 June 2026; 6sqft). Oscar Tang and Agnes Hsu-Tang also gave 150 works by Indigenous artists (The Art Newspaper, 16 June 2026).
funding_verdict: The New York Historical: mainly private gifts, with city and state money in its new wing
